In 2012, I got separated from my friends on the last night, but I decided to not let it get to me. I soldiered on and danced around like an idiot, getting white boy wasted and making friends with everyone I met. Eventually I got the attention of a group of very large gentlemen from Compton that were there to see Dre and Snoop. I noticed none of them had wristbands on, and they explained to me that they had rushed a fence with "some bitch-ass white boy" guarding it.

I was apparently hilariously intoxicated, because these fine sirs decided to adopt me into their crew. I followed them through the crowd (Surprisingly, people just let them pass, allll the way to the front) up to about 15 feet away from the stage and watched the most legendary show in rap history.

Then, it happened. "Yo Coachella... You know who this is!" That voice. No. It couldn't be. He's dead... But everyone always said it could be fake.. That he wanted out of the limelight. No way... All these years could it really have been? And I jumped on this dude (I think he told me his name was Murder) and clutched onto him with my arms and legs like a toddler hugs his momma and I screamed in my highest-pitched voice, "Tupac is ALIIIIIIVE!" And Murder screamed, in a shockingly higher voice, "OH MY GOD!" And we held each other and jumped up and down.. For a second. Until we realized what we were doing.

For a whole song, I thought he was real. His second song, he started to flicker. A gust of wind touched the projector and he did an unnatural slide, and we knew. Tupac's not alive, but I'll be damned if we didn't just see the world's first public show by a hologram. It was amazing. I lost Murder and the guys in the crowd after the show, but I found my friends back at camp and made then super jealous with this story.

I've been back to Coachella every year since.
